nutrient_reference_review._comment: Sources: National Institutes of Health Office of Dietary Supplements; Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics; National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine; explicitly unverified symptom patterns remain unknown.

energy_inadequate.context: Energy inadequacy concern: compare intake with documented needs, duration and weight trend; low intake alone does not establish malnutrition.

energy_excessive.context: Energy excess concern: require intake above documented needs; BMI or weight gain alone cannot establish excess.

protein_inadequate.context: Protein inadequacy concern: review intake, prescribed needs, muscle and wound findings; these findings alone do not establish protein deficiency.

protein_excessive.context: Protein excess concern: compare with prescribed targets and renal context; high intake alone does not establish organ injury.

carbohydrate_inadequate.context: Carbohydrate inadequacy concern: compare intake with documented needs and restrictions; do not infer hypoglycemia from an intake label.

carbohydrate_excessive.context: Carbohydrate excess concern: require intake evidence and actual targets; hyperglycemia alone cannot establish excessive carbohydrate intake.

fat_inadequate.context: Fat inadequacy concern: distinguish intake amount, fat type and absorption; do not infer fat-soluble vitamin deficiency.

fat_excessive.context: Fat excess concern: distinguish total amount and fat type; abnormal lipid values alone cannot establish dietary excess.

fluid_inadequate.context: Fluid inadequacy concern: review intake, orders, losses and hydration findings together; inadequate intake alone cannot establish dehydration.

fluid_excessive.context: Fluid excess concern: compare intake with documented orders and fluid shifts; edema alone cannot establish excessive intake.

fiber_inadequate.context: Fiber inadequacy concern: review actual intake and bowel findings; constipation alone cannot establish a dietary cause.

fiber_excessive.context: Fiber excess concern: review intake against prescribed needs and documented tolerance; do not manufacture gastrointestinal symptoms.

vitamin_c_inadequate.context: Vitamin C inadequacy concern: deficiency may accompany bruising or poor wound healing; check intake duration and other causes.

vitamin_c_excessive.context: Vitamin C excess concern: large supplement doses may cause diarrhea or cramps; verify dose and timing.

vitamin_d_inadequate.context: Vitamin D inadequacy concern: deficiency may impair bone mineralization; review recorded vitamin status, intake and absorption.

vitamin_d_excessive.context: Vitamin D excess concern: excess supplements may cause hypercalcemia with thirst or polyuria; verify exposure and recorded laboratories.

vitamin_e_inadequate.context: Vitamin E inadequacy concern: deficiency is rare and may involve neuropathy or weakness with fat malabsorption; review status and absorption.

vitamin_e_excessive.context: Vitamin E excess concern: high supplement doses may increase bleeding risk; verify dose and anticoagulant context.

vitamin_k_inadequate.context: Vitamin K inadequacy concern: deficiency may impair clotting; distinguish intake, absorption and anticoagulant effects.

vitamin_k_excessive.context: Vitamin K excess concern: no established toxicity pattern or upper limit exists for usual forms; review intake consistency with warfarin rather than invent toxicity.

thiamin_inadequate.context: Thiamin inadequacy concern: deficiency may accompany confusion, weakness or appetite loss; review intake duration, alcohol and documented clinical context.

thiamin_excessive.context: Thiamin excess concern: no established oral toxicity pattern or upper limit exists; verify exposure without treating absent limits as unlimited safety.

riboflavin_inadequate.context: Riboflavin inadequacy concern: deficiency may accompany cracked lips or mouth lesions; consider coexisting deficiencies and recorded dietary variety.

riboflavin_excessive.context: Riboflavin excess concern: adverse effects and an upper limit are not established; do not invent toxicity from dose alone.

niacin_inadequate.context: Niacin inadequacy concern: severe deficiency may cause a photosensitive rash; review intake and other nutrient contributors without diagnosing pellagra from rash alone.

niacin_excessive.context: Niacin excess concern: supplemental nicotinic acid may cause flushing or itching; distinguish form, dose and timing.

folate_inadequate.context: Folate inadequacy concern: deficiency may accompany megaloblastic anemia or oral lesions; review vitamin B12, intake and absorption.

folate_excessive.context: Folate excess concern: high supplemental folate may obscure hematologic evidence of vitamin B12 deficiency; review forms, doses and recorded vitamin status.

vitamin_b6_inadequate.context: Vitamin B6 inadequacy concern: deficiency may accompany glossitis or microcytic anemia; review other deficiencies, renal disease and medication context.

vitamin_b6_excessive.context: Vitamin B6 excess concern: chronic high supplement exposure may cause sensory neuropathy; verify dose, duration and competing explanations.

vitamin_b12_inadequate.context: Vitamin B12 inadequacy concern: deficiency may cause neurologic findings with or without anemia; consider absorption and medications even when intake is adequate.

vitamin_b12_excessive.context: Vitamin B12 excess concern: no established upper limit or typical toxicity pattern exists; an elevated serum result alone does not establish dietary excess.

pantothenic_acid_inadequate.context: Pantothenic acid inadequacy concern: deficiency is rare and may accompany burning extremities; review severe dietary restriction and other deficiencies.

pantothenic_acid_excessive.context: Pantothenic acid excess concern: very large supplement doses may cause diarrhea or gastrointestinal discomfort; verify exposure before attributing symptoms.

biotin_inadequate.context: Biotin inadequacy concern: rare deficiency may accompany hair loss or scaly rash; review intake and alternative causes.

biotin_excessive.context: Biotin excess concern: high supplements may distort laboratory assays despite no established toxicity limit; verify exposure before interpreting results.

calcium_inadequate.context: Calcium inadequacy concern: low serum calcium has multiple disease and medication causes; assess dietary adequacy separately from serum status.

calcium_excessive.context: Calcium excess concern: review supplement exposure and endocrine or renal causes of hypercalcemia; serum elevation alone cannot establish excessive intake.

iron_inadequate.context: Iron inadequacy concern: fatigue or weakness may accompany deficiency; review iron studies, inflammation, blood loss and intake together.

iron_excessive.context: Iron excess concern: high-dose supplements may cause gastrointestinal symptoms; verify dose and timing without inferring excess from symptoms alone.

magnesium_inadequate.context: Magnesium inadequacy concern: deficiency may cause weakness or cramps; review intake, gastrointestinal losses, renal losses and medications.

magnesium_excessive.context: Magnesium excess concern: supplements or medications may cause diarrhea and severe toxicity with impaired clearance; verify exposure and renal context.

potassium_inadequate.context: Potassium inadequacy concern: low serum potassium may involve losses or medications; weakness or arrhythmia does not establish inadequate intake.

potassium_excessive.context: Potassium excess concern: high serum potassium may reflect renal or medication effects even without excessive intake; review recorded exposure and clinical context.

phosphorus_inadequate.context: Phosphorus inadequacy concern: low phosphate may accompany weakness or bone pain but rarely reflects low intake alone; consider disease, shifts and nutrition-support context.

phosphorus_excessive.context: Phosphorus excess concern: high serum phosphate does not establish dietary excess; review renal function, additives and recorded prescription.

zinc_inadequate.context: Zinc inadequacy concern: deficiency may accompany diarrhea, hair loss or altered taste depending on age; review intake, absorption and alternatives.

zinc_excessive.context: Zinc excess concern: high supplement exposure may cause nausea or impair copper absorption; verify amount and duration.

fluoride_inadequate.context: Fluoride inadequacy concern: review water and dental exposure with caries history; caries alone does not establish inadequate dietary intake.

fluoride_excessive.context: Fluoride excess concern: excess exposure during tooth formation may cause fluorosis; verify childhood exposure rather than infer current intake.

copper_inadequate.context: Copper inadequacy concern: excess zinc can impair copper absorption; review recorded copper status, intake and absorption before inferring inadequacy.

copper_excessive.context: Copper excess concern: high exposure may cause gastrointestinal or liver injury; distinguish exposure from disorders of copper handling.

iodine_inadequate.context: Iodine inadequacy concern: deficiency may cause goiter or hypothyroidism; review intake and thyroid context without assigning a medical diagnosis.

iodine_excessive.context: Iodine excess concern: excess can also disturb thyroid function; distinguish intake, supplements and disease before selecting direction.

selenium_inadequate.context: Selenium inadequacy concern: deficiency is uncommon and context dependent; review documented status and nutrition exposure rather than infer a specific syndrome.

selenium_excessive.context: Selenium excess concern: chronic excess may cause hair or nail changes and garlic breath; verify supplement and food exposure.

manganese_inadequate.context: Manganese inadequacy concern: human deficiency signs are not firmly established; do not infer inadequacy from nonspecific findings.

manganese_excessive.context: Manganese excess concern: high environmental exposure may cause neurologic findings; distinguish occupational or water exposure from dietary intake.

chromium_inadequate.context: Chromium inadequacy concern: no definitive deficiency syndrome or validated status test exists in healthy populations; do not manufacture a diagnosis.

chromium_excessive.context: Chromium excess concern: toxicity evidence is limited and renal or liver disease may increase susceptibility; review supplement exposure without inventing a symptom pattern.

molybdenum_inadequate.context: Molybdenum inadequacy concern: acquired deficiency is exceptionally rare; review documented parenteral formulation rather than infer it from common symptoms.

molybdenum_excessive.context: Molybdenum excess concern: very high exposure has been associated with gout-like findings; verify exposure and alternative causes.

boron_inadequate.context: Boron inadequacy concern: human deficiency signs are not firmly established; do not infer a clinical deficiency.

boron_excessive.context: Boron excess concern: boric-acid or borax poisoning can cause gastrointestinal symptoms; distinguish toxic product exposure from ordinary dietary intake.

chloride_inadequate.context: Chloride inadequacy concern: interpret low serum chloride with losses, hydration and acid-base context; insufficient dietary intake remains unestablished without intake evidence.

chloride_excessive.context: Chloride excess concern: interpret high serum chloride with hydration, renal and treatment context; do not equate serum status with excessive dietary intake.

sodium_inadequate.context: Sodium inadequacy concern: interpret low serum sodium with fluid balance, losses and medications; low serum sodium alone cannot establish inadequate intake.

sodium_excessive.context: Sodium excess concern: compare intake with documented targets; blood pressure, edema or serum sodium alone cannot establish excessive intake.

sulfate_inadequate.context: Sulfate inadequacy concern: no specific dietary deficiency symptom pattern was verified for this library; require documented intake evidence and preserve uncertainty.

sulfate_excessive.context: Sulfate excess concern: no specific dietary excess symptom pattern was verified for this library; review documented substance, exposure and clinical context.

cobalt_inadequate.context: Cobalt inadequacy concern: no independent dietary deficiency symptom pattern was verified for this library; assess documented vitamin B12 context separately.

cobalt_excessive.context: Cobalt excess concern: no dietary excess symptom pattern was verified for this library; distinguish recorded exposure from assumptions about vitamin B12.

vitamin_a_inadequate.context: Vitamin A inadequacy concern: night blindness/xerophthalmia may accompany deficiency; check recorded intake and absorption context before attributing findings to low intake.

vitamin_a_excessive.context: Vitamin A excess concern: high preformed-vitamin doses may cause headache, blurred vision or nausea; verify exposure and form before attributing symptoms to excess.

sleep.edition: NHLBI sleep deficiency health effects checked 2026-10-28

cardiac.edition: AHA dietary guidance 2026; AHA/ACC/HFSA heart failure 2022

liver.edition: AASLD malnutrition, frailty and sarcopenia guidance 2021

energy.inadequate: Inadequate {nutrient}: compare recorded intake with documented needs; check duration, weight trend and barriers. Low intake alone is not malnutrition.
energy.excessive: Excessive {nutrient}: require intake above documented needs; BMI alone is not intake evidence. Check recorded meal patterns and contributors.

protein.inadequate: Inadequate {nutrient}: check documented protein intake, prescribed needs, muscle and wound findings. Do not infer low energy, deficiency or malnutrition.
protein.excessive: Excessive {nutrient}: compare with the actual prescribed target and relevant renal context. Protein intake alone does not establish organ injury.

carbohydrate.inadequate: Inadequate {nutrient}: compare reported intake with documented needs and restrictions. Do not infer hypoglycemia or a cause from the intake label.
carbohydrate.excessive: Excessive {nutrient}: use recorded intake and actual targets. Hyperglycemia alone cannot prove excess intake or nonadherence.

fat.inadequate: Inadequate {nutrient}: distinguish amount from type of fat and compare with recorded needs. Do not invent fat-soluble vitamin deficiency.
fat.excessive: Excessive {nutrient}: distinguish amount and types of fat. Lab lipids alone cannot prove excessive dietary intake.

fluid.inadequate: Inadequate {nutrient}: use reported intake, orders, losses and documented hydration findings. Do not diagnose dehydration from intake alone.
fluid.excessive: Excessive {nutrient}: compare intake with documented orders; consider recorded fluid shifts. Edema or weight gain alone does not prove excess intake.

fiber.inadequate: Inadequate {nutrient}: check recorded intake and bowel findings together. Constipation alone cannot establish a dietary cause.
fiber.excessive: Excessive {nutrient}: check actual intake, prescribed needs and documented tolerance. Do not manufacture GI symptoms.

vitamin.inadequate: Inadequate {nutrient}: intake below a documented target is not confirmed deficiency. Seek corresponding recorded labs, findings and contributors.
vitamin.excessive: Excessive {nutrient}: review recorded foods, supplements and doses against supplied standards. Excess intake alone does not prove toxicity.

mineral.inadequate: Inadequate {nutrient}: distinguish dietary intake from serum status and disease effects. Require documented nutrition findings; do not infer deficiency.
mineral.excessive: Excessive {nutrient}: check foods, supplements, prescribed targets and relevant disease context. A high serum value alone does not prove dietary excess.

behavior_cards.context: Tobacco: consider documented reflux, appetite, oral or intake findings; use only recorded links. Tobacco history alone is neither a nutrition problem nor proof of its cause.
Alcohol: assess recorded amount, meal displacement, intake and clinical findings. Do not label any use excessive or infer malnutrition, deficiency or liver disease.
Sleep/shift work: examine documented hunger, meal timing and intake patterns. The routine alone does not establish excess intake or the cause of a nutrition problem.
Meal pattern: inspect actual intake, frequency, duration and recorded barriers. Skipping a meal alone does not quantify a nutrient deficit or establish its cause.
Caffeine: use documented products, amounts, appetite, sleep and GI findings. Do not infer excessive use, appetite suppression or symptoms from a product name.

behavior_cards.conditions: \b(restrictive diet|crash diet|prolonged fasting|self.imposed restriction|avoids? food groups?)\b
behavior_cards.context: Restriction: distinguish prescribed, cultural, intentional and self-imposed patterns. Check documented adequacy; do not infer an eating disorder or deficiency.

Activity: consider Physical inactivity (NB) when inactivity is documented; physical limitations can be its recorded barrier. Cite activity findings and barrier separately; infer no intake direction or cause of weight change.
Supplements: check documented substance, dose and recorded effects/interactions. A supplement name alone cannot establish harm, excess or a medication interaction.
Adherence: require an existing agreed recommendation and a documented difficulty following it. Seek recorded access, belief, knowledge or practical barriers; do not assign blame.

cards.diagnosis: Glucose/A1c abnormalities do not establish excessive carbohydrate intake or poor adherence. Require dietary or behavioral evidence for those problems.
cards.monitoring: Use supplied glycemic targets. Glucose/A1c trends alone do not establish dietary adherence or overall recovery.

cards.diagnosis: Anemia, transfusion, erythropoietin treatment and dialysis can alter A1c interpretation. Do not attribute A1c alone to intake.
cards.monitoring: A1c may be affected by altered red-cell turnover; avoid attributing an isolated change to diet.

cards.diagnosis: Interpret potassium against supplied ranges and renal/medication context. Serum potassium alone does not establish inadequate or excessive intake; use documented contributors.
cards.monitoring: Interpret potassium against supplied ranges and renal context. A change does not establish a dietary cause; invent no food restrictions.

cards.diagnosis: Renal stage, dialysis and clinical stability change protein needs. Use the supplied prescription; kidney markers alone do not prove excessive protein intake.
cards.monitoring: Compare intake with the actual prescription. Do not carry predialysis protein restrictions into hemodialysis or infer kidney recovery from creatinine alone.

cards.diagnosis: CKD-related anemia may involve erythropoietin deficiency, iron availability, inflammation or other causes. Low hemoglobin alone does not prove inadequate iron intake.
cards.monitoring: Hemoglobin changes do not establish improved iron intake or correction of CKD-related anemia without supporting context.

cards.diagnosis: With heart failure or congestion, weight change may reflect fluid. Edema alone does not establish excessive fluid or sodium intake; use documented intake/orders.
cards.monitoring: Weight change may reflect fluid shifts rather than tissue gain/loss. Use documented edema, dry weight and prescribed limits; invent no fluid restriction.

cards.diagnosis: Abnormal lipids or blood pressure do not prove excessive fat/sodium intake. Require intake evidence and distinguish medication or disease context.
cards.monitoring: Describe supplied lipid/BP trends without attributing them solely to diet or changing prescribed targets.

cards.diagnosis: Surgery can affect intake, tolerance and needs. A postoperative label alone does not establish inadequate intake; use documented intake, duration and barriers.
cards.monitoring: Assess intake and tolerance against supplied recovery targets; surgery alone or one improving indicator does not establish nutritional recovery.

cards.diagnosis: Wound healing depends on adequate energy and protein. A wound does not prove inadequate intake or a specific micronutrient deficiency.
cards.monitoring: Describe documented intake and wound findings separately. Do not infer healing from protein intake alone or recommend unprovided supplements.

cards.diagnosis: Ascites/edema can mask tissue loss. Cirrhosis does not establish inadequate protein intake; assess documented intake and muscle findings.
cards.monitoring: Distinguish fluid-related weight change from tissue change. Follow supplied protein/fluid targets; do not infer recovery from albumin or impose protein restriction.

cards.diagnosis: Albumin/prealbumin are affected by inflammation, illness and hydration; they do not establish protein deficiency or malnutrition.
cards.monitoring: Albumin/prealbumin changes alone do not measure response to feeding or establish nutritional recovery.

cards.diagnosis: Adult GLIM requires phenotype plus etiology: nonvolitional loss, low BMI or assessed muscle loss AND sustained reduced intake/assimilation or inflammation. Use population/time criteria; missing data do not exclude malnutrition.
cards.monitoring: Describe supplied intake, weight and muscle findings; one improving marker does not establish resolution of malnutrition.
